change_summary: Created an isolated experiment copy of the backtester and added one new trade-specific exit branch for `trend_long` only: track day-1..3 adverse excursion versus the original stop distance, and when the trade has already taken `>=0.75R` early damage without reclaiming entry by the day-3 close, force a next-open discretionary exit (`trend_early_damage_exit`). No entry filters, ranking, sizing, LLM logic, or accepted repo code were changed.
component: experiment-only `quant/backtester_exp_20260422.py` (rolled back; no repo strategy code changed)

delta_metrics.note: Despite strong trade-level separation in the pre-screen, the portfolio-level rule failed across all three deterministic windows. The primary window lost a large slow-burn winner (`GOOG`) to the new early exit, while older windows added replacement-flow trades after early exits and still did not improve north-star EV.

hypothesis: A genuinely different `trend_long` exit may exist in early adverse-excursion damage rather than target-width or weak-close heuristics: if a fresh trend trade suffers `>=0.75R` intraday drawdown within its first 3 trading days and still closes at or below entry, schedule an exit at the next session open before the full stop is hit.
next_retry_requires: Do not retry another early-damage `trend_long` exit built only from first-3-day price path and original `R` distance
Treat `trade-level separation -> portfolio alpha` as a falsified shortcut for trend exits unless the next idea explains slot-allocation and slow-burn winner effects

If `trend_long` exit alpha is revisited again, it needs richer hold-quality context than pure OHLCV early-path damage (for example semantic/event context or another source that can distinguish slow winners from structurally broken trades)
notes: This experiment intentionally changed only one causal variable: a `trend_long` next-open exit after severe early adverse excursion. The code lived only in an isolated experiment copy and will not be kept.
rejection_reason: Rejected on Gate 4 multi-window stability. The rule regressed `expected_value_score` in the primary, bull, and weak windows, with materially worse Sharpe in every window. Trade-level loser markers did not translate into portfolio-level edge once slow winners and replacement-flow effects were included.
